summary: Neural architecture: frozen Qwen3-4B with float32 LoRA adapters and a zero-initialised cross-attention latent bridge; experience tokenizer with a separate exact-value channel; causal experiential core with gated persistent slots and a direct current-event path; decision trunk and unit-norm feature map; Bayesian fast state (exact Gaussian / NIG, Laplace GLM with censoring, forgetting, change detection) with a learned prior; CamLiveModel implementing nn.api.LatentModelAPI; measured presets 5M-1B; benchmark and fast-adaptation comparison with recorded evidence.

NA-01.limitations: Qwen/Qwen3-4B (4,022,468,096 parameters, bf16, frozen, pinned revision) is the only backbone loaded and tested; Qwen3-8B is a configuration change that was not run. Texts longer than max_text_tokens are cut to head 3/4 + tail 1/4 (counted in backbone.stats), not chunked. Single-stream generation speed is bounded by per-step Python overhead on this shared machine (on par with transformers' own generate, measured).

NA-02.limitations: Measured 50,953,765 experiential parameters (d_model 768, 6 blocks, 12 heads, d_ff 1024, 8 slots, 128 features); config.SCALE_PRESETS itself still holds d_ff=1792 (would give 67.8 M) - corrected inside nn/presets.py, change request A-1. The semantic projection of this preset is low-rank (7680 -> 384 -> 768).

NA-03.limitations: 16,713,856 adapter parameters = LoRA rank 32 on q_proj/v_proj of all 36 layers (11,796,480) + latent bridge (4,917,376). k_proj / o_proj / MLP projections carry no adapter in the default configuration.

NA-04.limitations: Reward and other-head counts are zero in the evidence file because those modules are registered by Workstreams B/C/D (register_head); count_parameters reports them per head once registered (tested with stand-in heads).

NA-05.limitations: Verified at initialisation and on small synthetic learning problems (8-step recall); whether the representations become useful abstractions that transfer across objectives is a question for training on real experience (Workstreams D / S), not shown here.

NA-07.limitations: One posterior per outcome kind (real, count, binary, time-to-event); categorical outcomes are not modelled by the fast layer (change request A-5). Non-Gaussian updates are Laplace approximations (exact mode, Gaussian shape). Time-to-event uses a constant-hazard (exponential) likelihood. Count over-dispersion is a single learned tempering factor.

NA-09.limitations: What is shown: on Qwen3-4B all 72 LoRA modules receive non-zero gradient through the embedding path (tokens -> core -> loss) and through generation_logprob, frozen weights have requires_grad=False and no .grad, and one optimizer step changes outputs. NOT shown here: adapter updates driven by real experience - the slow adapter schedule that calls these paths belongs to Workstream D.

NA-10.limitations: All presets are instantiated and counted on CPU; only the 50m preset was run on GPU (forward/backward step measured). The 150m-1b presets were never trained or benchmarked, and no learning-speed comparison across scales was made here.

NA-11.limitations: A token carries at most max_values (4) quantities; to_items continues longer lists in further items, while the candidate-action encoder keeps the first 4 cost quantities (dropped ones are counted in tokenizer.stats). Metric names are hashed into 2 x 2048 buckets (collisions possible). Relations and entities are text items; there is no graph structure.

NA-12.limitations: The bridge is cross-attention from the decoder's residual stream to bridge_tokens virtual prefix tokens, not tokens placed in the sequence (a literal zero prefix is not a no-op: measured logit change up to 1.0469; change request A-2). Shown: exact no-op at init, non-zero gradient, and that one optimisation step makes next-token probabilities depend on the latent. NOT shown: that a trained bridge improves the quality of generated candidate actions (needs training on experience; Workstreams B / D).

NA-13.limitations: See scientific_failures for where the learned prior loses (small support on Gaussian targets; fixed-noise variant; only a marginal lead on held-out counts). Synthetic meta-regression only (2-d inputs, 4 training and 3 held-out function families, 2 seeds, 600 evaluation tasks per split); it says nothing yet about real experience. The significance figures pool tasks that share one trained model per seed. Verdicts: {"gaussian": "held-out families: winner = learned_prior_bayes; ranking = ['learned_prior_bayes', 'blr_raw', 'gru', 'running_stats']; learned prior WINS", "count": "held-out families: winner = learned_prior_bayes; ranking = ['learned_prior_bayes', 'gru', 'blr_raw', 'running_stats']; learned prior WINS"}

config section 'nn' (all optional): see cam_live.nn.presets.NNConfig
not_done: Qwen3-8B (or any other backbone than Qwen/Qwen3-4B) was not loaded or tested; it is a configuration change only.

Presets 150m, 500m and 1b are instantiated and counted on CPU only: never trained, never run on GPU. No experiment here shows whether more experiential capacity helps (spec 16.10 asks for that comparison; it needs the learner and evaluation of Workstreams D / S).
config.SCALE_PRESETS (master-owned) still holds the overshooting d_ff values; the corrected numbers live in nn/presets.py (change request A-1).
The latent bridge is cross-attention to virtual prefix tokens, not prefix tokens inside the sequence (change request A-2). Its usefulness after training on experience is not evaluated here.

Adapter learning from real experience is not demonstrated here: only that both gradient paths work on the real backbone and that an optimizer step changes behaviour. The slow adapter schedule is Workstream D's.
The fast layer does not model categorical outcomes; time-to-event is constant-hazard only; one posterior per outcome kind (not per metric).
The fast-adaptation comparison is synthetic (no real experience data).
tokenize(with_grad=True) over whole contexts is memory-heavy; grad_last=k is provided but encode_decisions (master-owned) does not pass it yet (change request A-3).
No merged-LoRA inference path: with trained adapters generation is about 15 % slower than the bare backbone (measured); the tiny test backbone has no KV cache.
The backbone wrapper keeps the active bridge memory and capture buffers as instance state: one model must not run generation / embedding from several threads at once.
Long texts are truncated (head 3/4 + tail 1/4 of max_text_tokens), not chunked; truncation is counted in backbone.stats['truncated_tokens'].
scientific_failures: Gaussian targets, small support: the learned-prior Bayesian layer is WORSE than the recurrent baseline before it has seen about three points - held-out families NLL at k=0: 1.6995 vs GRU 1.4188 vs running statistics 1.467 (a unit normal scores 1.4189); at k=1: 1.5156 vs GRU 1.3854; in-distribution k=0: 1.6896 vs GRU 1.3495. It wins from k=3 on (k=3: 1.3269 vs 1.3325; k=8: 1.0869 vs 1.1449; k=31: 0.6137 vs 1.0467). Cause: the conjugate normal-inverse-gamma prior ties the weight uncertainty to the uncertain noise scale, which makes the prior predictive heavy-tailed. (docs/evidence/A/fast_adaptation.json)

Gaussian targets, fixed learned noise instead of inferred noise: FAILS on held-out families - mean NLL 1.9933 (per seed [1.9935, 1.9931]) vs 0.8909 with inferred noise, and worse than running statistics (1.4483); it becomes over-confident as evidence accumulates (k=31: 2.1035). In-distribution it is calibrated at k=0 (1.3458) but still behind overall (0.2988 vs 0.2132). The inferred-noise mode is therefore the default. (docs/evidence/A/fast_adaptation_noise_mode.json)

Count targets, held-out families: the learned-prior layer is only marginally ahead of the GRU with a negative-binomial head - mean NLL 2.6201 vs 2.6381 (difference -0.018 +- 0.0078, z = -2.31 with tasks pooled over 2 seeds), and the GRU is ahead at the largest support size (k=31: 2.4892 vs 2.5073; RMSE 18.1002 vs 18.2307). This is not a robust win. An earlier run in which the GRU had a plain Poisson head (no way to express uncertainty) showed a large gap (GRU 3.82) that was an artefact of that head; the head was corrected before the recorded run.
